## 3dslibris 3.1.0

This release focuses on the things you do every time you read: starting the app, browsing your library, opening a book and turning pages. Search, illustrations and PDF/CBZ reading also get a round of performance improvements.

### Startup and library

- Read preferences before loading fonts and discovering books, so your configured fonts and saved reading state are used from the start. Avoid loading fallback fonts twice and load monospaced faces only when needed.
- Keep custom font directories working even when they do not contain the bundled fonts. Preserve the bundled fallback after rejecting an invalid font selection.
- Reuse the boot splash between unchanged startup steps, skip redundant font-file checks after successful initialization, and defer browser covers when reopening the last book.
- Add a consolidated metadata index for title/author sorting. It reads cached metadata sequentially instead of opening a separate `.bmc` for every indexed book. Source size and date are still checked, and missing or damaged index entries fall back to the individual caches.
- Keep root-library entries while browsing folders, defer metadata reads for filename/date sorting, and filter directory entries before querying their file state.
- Load and retain covers for visible entries, defer folder-cover discovery until requested, and reuse cover paths and the in-memory cover-cache index. Cache pruning and thumbnail retries avoid repeated directory work.
- Reuse four gallery buttons instead of allocating one per book. Avoid repeated button-label layout, unchanged marquee frames, and redundant browser clears and splash draws.
- Restore saved bookmarks without duplicating them during startup.

### Opening books and turning pages

- Check usable EPUB page caches before opening the archive. Reuse ZIP entry positions and replay the CSS head prefix from the same content stream instead of reading it again.
- Reduce repeated UTF-8 decoding and shaping for ordinary left-to-right text, including accented text. Reuse paragraph-layout work and avoid copying XML class attributes just to resolve CSS.
- Reduce MOBI opening memory peaks by releasing decompressed buffers earlier, skipping unnecessary cleanup copies, repairing text in place, and processing paragraph wraps without retaining every line.
- Avoid asynchronous setup when workers are disabled.
- Clip glyphs before their pixel loops and copy fully opaque glyph pixels without alpha blending. Reuse font-face lookups and cached Latin-1 glyph pointers within the existing glyph-cache budget.
- Resize only the font faces being used, and reuse prepared FreeType sizes when switching between body text and superscripts/subscripts.
- Cache up to 128 centered/right-aligned line measurements for the last drawn page. Redraws reuse their widths while positions still follow the current margins and screen geometry.
- Reduce duplicate page clears and framebuffer fills. Convert pixels in contiguous spans and track pending partial updates separately for both physical framebuffer buffers.

### PDF, CBZ and XPS

- Build page-fit PDF previews from the full-page interactive raster when available, preserving the complete page and its margins without scanning every preview pixel for ink bounds.
- Reuse the CBZ reader's MuPDF decoding context between pages, while releasing decoded-image references and borrowed archive data safely.
- Share the RGB565 scaler and use integer interpolation weights. Avoid redundant background fills and derive the logical screen mirror from the native wide-screen render instead of scaling it twice.
- During PDF/CBZ panning, restore the previous viewport border strips instead of repainting the full lower preview. Page, theme, orientation, zoom and content changes still invalidate the panel when needed.
- Draw the HUD after the page in the same frame, keeping the clock and page counter visible without forcing a full preview repaint on the next pan.
- Preserve color rendering, page proportions and native wide-screen detail.

### Search and illustrations

- Scan search annotations sequentially, use bounded work slices with cancellation checks, and handle simple ASCII through a shorter matching path. Unicode normalization and word-boundary behavior are preserved.
- Reuse up to 1 MiB of compressed image data between viewer zoom operations. Keep unchanged controls and help text while panning.
- Probe raster headers only when an SVG wrapper needs disambiguation. Decode known inline-image layouts at their final size and reuse bounded scaling coordinates.
- Use direct conversion for native-size rasters and skip unnecessary blending for opaque pixels.
- Store opaque inline images as RGB565 and copy them by row, halving their retained pixel storage. Transparent images still blend against the actual screen contents. The inline cache keeps its 1 MiB limit and accounts for both representations.

### Updating and testing

Reading progress, bookmarks and preferences are kept. The metadata index is built from existing caches as needed and is removed by the existing clear-cache action. Its first migration can still read the individual `.bmc` files.

Host regression tests cover cache migration/corruption, real FreeType and MuPDF paths, allocation failures, image pixels, and preview/HUD redraws. Console timing, HOME and suspend/resume still need hardware testing; there is no promised percentage speedup. See the [performance and regression checklist](https://github.com/RigleGit/3dslibris/blob/main/docs/PERFORMANCE_SMOKE_TEST.md) to compare cold and cached runs.

Native `GSP_RGB565_OES` display framebuffers remain follow-up work. This release keeps the existing display-output format and does not enable background workers or move rendering to the GPU.

### Downloads

- `3dslibris.cia` or `3dslibris.3dsx` for normal use.
- `3dslibris-sdmc.zip`: runtime files for Homebrew Launcher installs; use with the `.3dsx` download.
- Debug builds (`3dslibris-debug.cia` / `3dslibris-debug.3dsx`) and `3dslibris-source.tar.gz` are also included.

Thanks to everyone reporting issues and trying the new builds. You can support the project with a ⭐ on GitHub or [a coffee](https://ko-fi.com/rigle).
